results.title: JUSAG defends indefinite strike, says government had 10 months to resolve salary concerns
results.content: The Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) has defended its decision to embark on an indefinite strike, saying it gave the government 10 months to resolve concerns over its reviewed salaries and allowances before resorting to industrial action. The association's General Secretary, Abdulai Yakubu, said members had exercised restraint despite the financial difficulties they were facing and expected the government to demonstrate empathy by addressing their demands. Speaking on JoyNews, Mr Yakubu said the strike would not prevent the association from engaging the government to resolve the dispute. "Engaging the government doesn't depend on putting the strike on hold. The strike can be in force and then we engage government. We have considered the impact of the strike on the ordinary Ghanaian and decided to restrain ourselves for 10 whole months," he said.

results.title: Gold mining formalisation must not legitimise environmental destruction – CLGB
results.content: The Chamber of Licensed Gold Buyers (CLGB) has urged the government to adopt a conditional and evidence-based approach to formalising Ghana’s artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) sector, warning against granting legitimacy to operations that cause environmental destruction. The Chamber says the GoldBod-led formalisation programme presents an opportunity to address longstanding challenges in the sector through an accessible, transparent and enforceable regulatory framework. However, in a policy statement, it stressed that government must distinguish between mining operations that can be conducted lawfully and responsibly and those that threaten water bodies, forests, agricultural lands and public health.

results.title: North Tongu residents expected at Yɛ Gye Yɛ Sika demonstration – Senyo Amekpulenu
results.content: Residents of North Tongu and persons displaced by the Akosombo Dam spillage are expected to join the Y3 Gye Y3 Sika demonstration in Accra on Tuesday, November 3, the Volta Regional Youth Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Emmanuel Senyo Amekpulenu, has said. The protest, scheduled to begin at 6:00 a.m., is expected to bring together young people and other concerned groups to demand accountability over reported financial discrepancies. Speaking on The AM Show with Maame Esi Nyamekye Thompson, Mr Amekpulenu said the demonstration would also provide an opportunity for residents affected by the Akosombo spillage to demand funds intended to support their recovery and rebuild structures destroyed by the disaster.

results.title: Government plans free tertiary education, 5% jobs quota for persons with disabilities
results.content: The government has announced plans to introduce free tertiary education for persons with disabilities and enforce a minimum five per cent employment quota in public and private institutions as part of efforts to improve their participation in national development. The proposed interventions form part of a broader disability inclusion agenda outlined by the Policy Advisor to the Vice President, Dr Samuel Ofosu Ampofo, at the Day of Help for Persons with Disabilities in Koforidua on Friday, October 30, 2026. Representing Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang, Dr Ofosu Ampofo said the government was committed to ensuring that persons with disabilities had equal opportunities in education, employment and other areas of national life. He said disability inclusion should be treated not as an act of charity but as a fundamental human rights issue.
